facts.statement: In 2020, a re-evaluation questioned the previous referral and named it a distinct species in a new genus.
facts.quote: In 2020, a re-evaluation questioned the referral and named it as a distinct species in a new genus.

facts.statement: It lived approximately 75 million years ago during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 75 millones de años durante el Campaniense, en lo que es hoy Norteamérica

facts.statement: The name means "star lizard," referencing its head ornamentation and the David Bowie song "Starman."
facts.quote: Stellasaurus (meaning "star lizard"; both in reference to the shape of its head ornamentation and as an homage to the song "Starman" by David Bowie)

facts.statement: Stellasaurus had complex cranial ornamentation like other ceratopsid dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Like other ceratopsid dinosaurs, Stellasaurus would have had complex cranial ornamentation.

facts.statement: It possessed a very long nasal horn that was larger than that found in Centrosaurus.
facts.quote: Like the former, it possessed a very long nasal horn, larger than that found in Centrosaurus.

facts.statement: The nasal horn was erect, recurved (pointing inwards), and compressed laterally.
facts.quote: This horn is erect and recurved (pointed inwards, unlike the very procurved horn of Einiosaurus which points in the opposite direction) and compressed, laterally.

facts.statement: Its parietal anatomy featured long, straight third and fourth spines, with the fifth through seventh spines not elongated.
facts.quote: Its parietal anatomy is much more similar to Einiosaurus, with long, straight third parietal spines, similarly straight fourth parietal spines less than half the size of these, and fifth through seventh ones not elongated at all.

facts.statement: No separate frill ossifications (epiparietals or episquamosals) have been found, suggesting these genera may have lacked them.
facts.quote: Similar to Einiosaurus and Achelousaurus, no epiparietals or episquamosals, in the sense of separate "frill ossifications", have been found, indicating the three genera may have lacked them.

facts.statement: Contemporary dinosaurs included hadrosaurids, ankylosaurs, the tyrannosaurid Daspletosaurus (a ceratopsian specialist), and smaller theropods.
facts.quote: Dinosaurs that lived alongside Stellasaurus include the basal ornithopod Orodromeus, hadrosaurids (such as Hypacrosaurus, Maiasaura, and Prosaurolophus), the centrosaurines Brachyceratops and Einiosaurus, the leptoceratopsid Cerasinops, the ankylosaurs Edmontonia and Euoplocephalus, the tyrannosaurid Daspletosaurus (which appears to have been a specialist of preying on ceratopsians), as well as the smaller theropods Bambiraptor, Chirostenotes, Troodon, and Avisaurus.

facts.statement: Stellasaurus is classified within the subfamily Centrosaurinae of the family Ceratopsidae.
facts.quote: Stellasaurus is placed within the Ceratopsidae in the Centrosaurinae.

facts.statement: The type and only known species is Stellasaurus ancellae.
facts.quote: The type and only species is Stellasaurus ancellae.

facts.statement: Researchers differ in their interpretation of the fossil, specifically regarding the position of the neck shield and parietal spines.
facts.quote: Wilson and Ryan differ from other researchers in their interpretation of the fossil.

facts.statement: There is a debate regarding the count of epiparietalia, with Andrew McDonald identifying P8 and Wilson et al. identifying P7.
facts.quote: Another point of contention is the count of the epiparietalia. According to Andrew McDonald the frost is epiparietal the P8, but according to Wilson, Ryan & Evans it is the P7.

facts.statement: Wilson et al. do not consider separate skin ossifications (osteoderms) to have been demonstrated in Styracosaurus, Stellasaurus, and Einiosaurus.
facts.quote: They do not consider these to have been demonstrated in Styracosaurus, Stellasaurus and Einiosaurus.

facts.statement: The describers view it as a transitional form between Styracosaurus albertensis and Einiosaurus on a lineage leading to Achelousaurus and Pachyrhinosaurus.
facts.quote: The describers saw it as a transitional form between Styracosaurus albertensis and Einiosaurus on a single evolutionary line that led to Achelousaurus and Pachyrhinosaurus.

facts.statement: Fossil remains of Stellasaurus were discovered in Montana, USA, in the Late Campanian Two Medicine Formation of the Upper Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Sus restos fósiles se descubrieron en Montana, Estados Unidos durante el Cretácico Superior en la Formación Two Medicine del Campaniano tardío

facts.statement: The specimens were originally proposed as a distinct taxon in 1992 before being assigned to Rubeosaurus.
facts.quote: Originalmente propuesto como un taxón distinto en 1992, los especímenes fueron luego asignados a Rubeosaurus.

facts.statement: In 2020, a re-evaluation questioned the assignment to Rubeosaurus and named it a distinct species in a new genus.
facts.quote: En 2020, una revaluación cuestionó la asignación al mismo y la nombró como una especie distinta en un nuevo género.

facts.statement: The genus name Stellasaurus refers to the star-like shape of its head ornamentation and honors David Bowie's song "Starman".
facts.quote: Su nombre de género Stellasaurus, del latín Stella por estrella y saurus del griego reptil hace tanto referencia a la forma de la ornamentación de su cabeza como en homenaje a la canción "Starman" de David Bowie.

facts.statement: The describers described the animal as a transitional form between Styracosaurus and Einiosaurus within a single evolutionary line leading to Achelousaurus and Pachyrhinosaurus.
facts.quote: Los descriptores lo describieron como una forma de transición entre Styracosaurus y Einiosaurus en una sola línea evolutiva que condujo a Achelousaurus y Pachyrhinosaurus.

facts.statement: The describers view the species as an intermediate between Styracosaurus albertensis and Einiosaurus, not closely related to Rubeosaurus ovatus, which they consider a species of Styracosaurus.
facts.quote: Los descriptores ven a la especie como un intermedio entre Styracosaurus albertensis y Einiosaurus, y no estrechamente relacionada con Rubeosaurus ovatus, que los descriptores consideran una especie de Styracosaurus.

facts.statement: The authors reject the interpretation that ceratopsid evolution in these formations occurred as a succession of branching divisions.
facts.quote: Los autores descartan una interpretación de la evolución de los ceratópsidos en estas formaciones como una sucesión de divisiones.

facts.statement: Stellasaurus lived during the Campanian stage, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group of Stellasaurus is the subfamily Centrosaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Centrosaurinae

facts.statement: Stellasaurus belongs to the family Ceratopsidae.
facts.quote: Family: Ceratopsidae

facts.statement: Stellasaurus is classified in the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Stellasaurus is Stellasaurus ancellae.
facts.quote: Type species: Stellasaurus ancellae

facts.statement: It is debated whether the argument for a direct lineage is more probable than branching models, as critics argue that ancestors and extinction are implied in branching models anyway.
facts.quote: A esta línea de razonamiento se le suele objetar que dada la existencia de una segunda rama, el ancestro y la extinción ya están implícitos y por tanto no la hacen más improbable.
